questions.stem: Èwo nínú àwọn orí-ọ̀rọ̀ wọ̀nyí ni a lè fi kọ àròkọ aṣàpèjúwe tó dára jù?
options: Ọjọ́ tí mo kọ́kọ́ wọ ọkọ̀ òfuurufú
Ìwé kíkà dára ju iṣẹ́ ọwọ́ lọ
Bí a ṣe ń gbin àgbàdo
questions.explanation: A descriptive essay (aṣàpèjúwe) describes a place, person or thing, e.g. the hospital in my town.

questions.stem: Àròkọ tí ó ń ṣàlàyé bí a ṣe ń ṣe nǹkan, bí 'Bí a ṣe ń se ẹ̀wà', jẹ́ àròkọ
questions.explanation: An essay explaining a process is expository (ajẹmọ́-ìṣípayá).

questions.stem: Èwo ni kò yẹ kí ó wà nínú lẹ́tà àìgbẹ̀fẹ́?
options: Àdírẹ́sì ẹni tí a kọ ọ́ sí
questions.explanation: A formal letter (àìgbẹ̀fẹ́) avoids jokes and casual language but has addresses, date and a heading.

questions.stem: Àròkọ aṣàríyànjiyàn máa ń ní
options: ìtàn ohun tí ó ṣẹlẹ̀ lẹ́sẹẹsẹ
ìlànà bí a ṣe ń se oúnjẹ
ẹ̀gbẹ́ méjì tí ó ń tako ara wọn
questions.explanation: An argumentative essay weighs two opposing sides of an issue.

questions.stem: Mélòó ni fáwẹ̀lì àìránmúpè tí ó wà nínú èdè Yorùbá?
questions.explanation: Yoruba has seven oral vowels: a, e, ẹ, i, o, ọ, u.

questions.stem: Èwo ni fáwẹ̀lì ẹ̀yìn?
questions.explanation: Back vowels are u, o, ọ; i, e, ẹ are front and a is central.

questions.stem: Ọ̀rọ̀ wo ni ó ní ìlànà ohùn ìsàlẹ̀-òkè?
questions.explanation: ìwé is low-high; ilé is mid-high, ọkọ̀ mid-low, àgbà low-low and ọmọ mid-mid.

questions.stem: Ìyàtọ̀ ìtumọ̀ tí ó wà láàárín 'ọkọ', 'ọkọ̀' àti 'ọkọ́' wá láti ọ̀dọ̀
questions.explanation: The three words (husband, vehicle, hoe) differ only in tone.

questions.stem: Tí a bá pín ọ̀rọ̀ 'àgbàlagbà' sí sílébù, iye sílébù tí a ó rí ni
questions.explanation: à-gbà-la-gbà has four syllables.

questions.stem: Ìhun sílébù ọ̀rọ̀ 'ọmọdé' ni
questions.explanation: ọ-mọ-dé: a vowel syllable followed by two consonant-vowel syllables.

questions.stem: Èwo ni kọ́ńsónáǹtì àfeyínfètèpè?
questions.explanation: [f] is produced with the lower lip against the upper teeth (labiodental).

questions.stem: Nígbà tí 'gbé omi' di 'gbómi', ìlànà ìró tí ó wáyé ni
questions.explanation: The vowel e of gbé is deleted (vowel elision) when the words join.

questions.stem: Nínú gbólóhùn 'Tolú ra aṣọ tuntun lánàá', ọ̀rọ̀-ìṣe ni
questions.explanation: ra (buy) is the verb.

questions.stem: Nínú gbólóhùn 'Àwọn ọmọ náà ti jẹun', 'ti' fi hàn pé iṣẹ́ náà
questions.explanation: ti marks the perfect (completed action).

questions.stem: 'Márùndínlógún' túmọ̀ sí
questions.explanation: Márùndínlógún is twenty minus five: 15.

questions.stem: Èwo ni ó túmọ̀ sí 19?
questions.explanation: Mọ́kàndínlógún is twenty minus one: 19; Mọ́kànlélógún is 21 and Méjìdínlógún 18.

questions.stem: Nínú 'aṣọ funfun', 'funfun' jẹ́
questions.explanation: funfun (white) describes the noun aṣọ: an adjective.

questions.stem: Èwo nínú àwọn ọ̀rọ̀ wọ̀nyí ni a ṣẹ̀dá pẹ̀lú àfòmọ́ 'oní-'?
questions.explanation: oní + ṣòwò gives oníṣòwò (trader).

questions.stem: Ọ̀rọ̀-arọ́pò-orúkọ ẹnì kẹta ọ̀pọ̀ ni
questions.explanation: wọ́n is third person plural; a is first plural, ẹ second plural, mo first singular, ó third singular.

questions.stem: Nínú gbólóhùn 'Adé lọ sí Èkó', 'sí' jẹ́
questions.explanation: sí introduces the destination: a preposition (atọ́kùn).

questions.stem: Gbólóhùn wo ni ó wà ní àsìkò ọjọ́-iwájú?
options: Mo máa ń lọ sí oko
Èmi yóò lọ sí oko lọ́la
questions.explanation: yóò marks the future.

questions.stem: Ewì tí àwọn olùsìn Ṣàngó máa ń kọ ni
questions.explanation: Ṣàngó pípè is chanted by Ṣàngó devotees.

questions.stem: Ìrèmọ̀jé jẹ́ ewì tí àwọn ọdẹ máa ń sun níbi
questions.explanation: Ìrèmọ̀jé is the funeral chant for a dead hunter.

questions.stem: Ewì ìyìn tí a fi ń ṣàpèjúwe ìdílé tàbí ènìyàn kan ni
questions.explanation: Oríkì is praise poetry for a person, lineage or town.

questions.stem: Ọ̀rọ̀ tí oníṣègùn máa ń pè láti mú kí oògùn ṣiṣẹ́ ni
questions.explanation: Ọfọ̀ is incantation used to activate medicine.

questions.stem: Àpapọ̀ iye Odù Ifá (Ojú Odù àti Ọmọ Odù) jẹ́
questions.explanation: Sixteen principal Odù combine to give 16 x 16 = 256 Odù.

questions.stem: Ohun èlò tí babaláwo máa ń fi ìyẹ̀rosùn sí lórí láti dá Ifá ni
questions.explanation: Divination powder (ìyẹ̀rosùn) is spread on the divination tray (ọpọ́n Ifá).

questions.stem: Ìtàn tí àwọn àgbà máa ń pa fún àwọn ọmọdé ní alẹ́, tí orin sì máa ń wà nínú rẹ̀, ni
questions.explanation: Àlọ́ àpagbè is the folktale with songs; àlọ́ àpamọ̀ is the riddle.

questions.stem: Ìwé ìtàn àròsọ ọ̀tẹlẹ̀múyẹ́ 'Àjà Ló Lẹrù' jẹ́ iṣẹ́
questions.explanation: Àjà Ló Lẹrù, a detective novel, was written by Ọládẹ̀jọ Òkédìjí.

questions.stem: Ta ni ó kọ ìwé ìtàn àròsọ 'Ó Le Kú'?
questions.explanation: Ó Le Kú is a novel by Akínwùmí Ìṣọ̀lá.

questions.stem: Ọ̀nà-èdè tí a fi ń fún ohun aláìlẹ́mìí ní ìwà ènìyàn ni
questions.explanation: Personification (ìfohunpènìyàn) gives human qualities to non-living things.

questions.stem: Ẹni tí ó kọ ìwé ni a ń pè ní
questions.explanation: The author is òǹkọ̀wé; akéwì is a poet, òṣèré an actor and atẹ̀wé a printer.

questions.stem: Ìtàn tí a kọ sílẹ̀ láti ṣe lórí ìtàgé ni
questions.explanation: A story written to be acted on stage is a play (eré-onítàn).

questions.stem: Ọ̀nà tí ọmọbìnrin Yorùbá fi ń kí bàbá rẹ̀ láàárọ̀ ni
questions.explanation: Women kneel (ìkúnlẹ̀) to greet elders; men prostrate (ìdọ̀bálẹ̀).

questions.stem: Oúnjẹ tí a fi ewùrà ṣe ni
questions.explanation: Ọ̀jọ̀jọ̀ is made from grated water yam (ewùrà).

questions.stem: Ọmọ tí a bí tẹ̀lé Ìdòwú ni a ń pè ní
questions.explanation: Àlàbá is the child born after Ìdòwú.

questions.stem: Bí a ṣe ń kí ẹni tí ó ń ṣiṣẹ́ lọ́wọ́ ni
questions.explanation: Ẹ kú iṣẹ́ greets someone at work.

questions.stem: Ọba ìlú Ọ̀yọ́ ni a ń pè ní
questions.explanation: The Aláàfin rules Ọ̀yọ́; the Ọọ̀ni rules Ifẹ̀ and the Awùjalẹ̀ Ìjẹ̀bú-Òde.

questions.stem: Ètò tí àwọn àgbẹ̀ fi ń ṣiṣẹ́ lóko ara wọn lẹ́nìkọ̀ọ̀kan ní àyípo ni
questions.explanation: Àáró is rotational mutual-aid labour; èésú is a rotating savings scheme.

questions.stem: Òrìṣà tí àwọn olùsìn rẹ̀ máa ń wọ aṣọ funfun, tí a sì gbàgbọ́ pé ó ń mọ ènìyàn, ni
questions.explanation: Ọbàtálá, the moulder of human bodies, is associated with white cloth.

questions.stem:
Yan ọ̀kan nínú àwọn orí-ọ̀rọ̀ wọ̀nyí, kí o sì kọ àròkọ tí ó tó ọ̀ọ́dúnrún ọ̀rọ̀ lé e lórí:
(a) Ọdún ìbílẹ̀ kan tí mo gbádùn jùlọ.
(b) Àǹfààní àti àléébù ẹ̀rọ ìbánisọ̀rọ̀ alágbèéká.
(c) Lẹ́tà sí ọ̀gá ilé-ìwé rẹ láti tọrọ ààyè ọjọ́ mẹ́ta. [25 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
10 marks: Content (Àkóónú): relevant, well-developed ideas suited to the essay type chosen
5 marks: Organisation (Ìhun): introduction, logical paragraphs, conclusion; formal letter layout with addresses, date, salutation and closing for (c)
7 marks: Expression (Ìlò èdè): idiomatic Yoruba with apt proverbs and varied sentences
3 marks: Mechanical accuracy: official orthography, tone marks and punctuation
questions.explanation: (a) is narrative or descriptive, (b) argumentative/expository, (c) a formal letter. A good answer plans an introduction, focused paragraphs and a conclusion, uses idiomatic Yoruba with proverbs and marks tones correctly.

questions.stem:
(a) Kí ni fáwẹ̀lì? [2 marks]
(b) Pín fáwẹ̀lì àìránmúpè méjèèje èdè Yorùbá sí ìsọ̀rí ní ìbámu pẹ̀lú ipò ahọ́n (iwájú, àárín, ẹ̀yìn). [7 marks]
(c) Kọ ohùn mẹ́ta èdè Yorùbá, kí o sì fún ọ̀kọ̀ọ̀kan ní àmì rẹ̀ àti àpẹẹrẹ ọ̀rọ̀ kan. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: A vowel is a speech sound produced without obstruction of air in the mouth
3 marks: Front (iwájú): i, e, ẹ
1 mark: Central (àárín): a
3 marks: Back (ẹ̀yìn): u, o, ọ
2 marks: High tone (ohùn òkè), marked with an acute accent, e.g. bá
2 marks: Mid tone (ohùn àárín), usually unmarked, e.g. ba
2 marks: Low tone (ohùn ìsàlẹ̀), marked with a grave accent, e.g. bà
questions.explanation: Vowels are produced with free airflow. Front: i, e, ẹ; central: a; back: u, o, ọ. Tones are high (´), mid (unmarked) and low (`), e.g. bá, ba, bà.

questions.stem:
(a) Kí ni àfòmọ́? [3 marks]
(b) Fún àpẹẹrẹ ọ̀rọ̀ méjì tí a ṣẹ̀dá pẹ̀lú ọ̀kọ̀ọ̀kan àwọn àfòmọ́ ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ wọ̀nyí: (i) oní- (ii) àì- (iii) olù- (iv) a-. [8 marks]
(c) Ṣàlàyé ìyàtọ̀ tí ó wà láàárín 'ti' àti 'ń' nínú gbólóhùn, kí o sì fún ọ̀kọ̀ọ̀kan ní àpẹẹrẹ. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: An affix (àfòmọ́) is a bound element attached to a root to form a new word
2 marks: oní-: e.g. oníṣòwò, onílù, onímọ̀ (any two)
2 marks: àì-: e.g. àìsàn, àìmọ̀, àìlera (any two)
2 marks: olù-: e.g. olùkọ́, olùfẹ́, olùgbàlà (any two)
2 marks: a-: e.g. akọ̀wé, apẹja, akọrin (any two)
2 marks: ti marks completed (perfect) action, e.g. Ó ti jẹun
2 marks: ń marks continuing (progressive) action, e.g. Ó ń jẹun
questions.explanation: An affix attaches to a root to derive words: oníṣòwò, àìsàn, olùkọ́, akọ̀wé. 'ti' shows completed action; 'ń' shows ongoing action.

questions.stem:
(a) Kí ni oríkì? [3 marks]
(b) Dárúkọ oríṣi oríkì mẹ́ta. [3 marks]
(c) Ṣàlàyé ìwúlò oríkì mẹ́ta láwùjọ Yorùbá. [9 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: Oríkì is praise poetry describing the qualities, deeds or origin of a person, lineage, town or deity
1 mark: Oríkì orílẹ̀ (lineage praise)
1 mark: Oríkì ènìyàn/àbísọ, e.g. Àkàndé, Àyìnkẹ́
1 mark: Oríkì ìlú or oríkì òrìṣà
3 marks: Encourages and spurs a person to bravery or good deeds
3 marks: Preserves history of families and towns
3 marks: Used for greeting, pampering and showing affection; entertainment at ceremonies
questions.explanation: Oríkì praises people, lineages, towns and deities. It inspires, records family and town history, and is used to greet, pamper and entertain.

questions.stem:
(a) Ṣàlàyé ìyàtọ̀ tí ó wà láàárín ìtàn àròsọ, eré-onítàn àti ewì àpilẹ̀kọ. [9 marks]
(b) Ṣàlàyé ọ̀nà-èdè mẹ́ta tí òǹkọ̀wé lè lò, kí o sì fún ọ̀kọ̀ọ̀kan ní àpẹẹrẹ. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: Ìtàn àròsọ: prose narrative told in paragraphs and chapters by a narrator
3 marks: Eré-onítàn: written to be performed, in dialogue between characters, divided into scenes or acts
3 marks: Ewì àpilẹ̀kọ: written in lines and stanzas with rhythm and condensed language
2 marks: First figure of speech correctly explained with example, e.g. àfiwé tààrà
2 marks: Second figure correctly explained with example, e.g. àsọdùn
2 marks: Third figure correctly explained with example, e.g. ìfohunpènìyàn
questions.explanation: Prose fiction narrates in paragraphs; drama is dialogue for the stage; poetry uses lines and stanzas. Figures include simile, hyperbole and personification, each illustrated.

questions.stem:
(a) Ṣàlàyé ètò ìgbéyàwó ní ilẹ̀ Yorùbá láti ìgbà tí ọkùnrin bá rí obìnrin tí ó wù ú títí di ọjọ́ ìgbéyàwó. [10 marks]
(b) Kí ni iṣẹ́ alárinà nínú ètò ìgbéyàwó? [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Courtship (ìfẹ́sọ́nà) after the man sees a woman he likes
2 marks: Use of a go-between (alárinà) and family inquiries (ìwádìí), sometimes consulting Ifá
2 marks: Formal request and consent (ìtọrọ and ìjọ́hẹ́n)
2 marks: Bride-price ceremony (ìdána) with items presented
2 marks: Wedding day: bride escorted to the husband's house, ẹkún ìyàwó, prayers and feasting
2 marks: Alárinà links the two families and carries messages
2 marks: Makes inquiries about the families' backgrounds and settles misunderstandings
1 mark: Stands as witness and guarantor of the marriage
questions.explanation: Traditional marriage passes through courtship, inquiry with a go-between, formal request and consent, ìdána, and the wedding when the bride is escorted to her husband's home. The alárinà links the families, investigates backgrounds, settles disputes and witnesses the marriage.
